key_insight: This paper argues that subquadratic sequence models can offer a practical alternative to Transformers for long-context tasks, but their effectiveness depends on the architectural choice. By comparing xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet, it highlights which designs better preserve performance while reducing compute.
problem_solved: It addresses the high computational and memory cost of Transformer attention, especially for long sequences, and asks which subquadratic architecture is most effective for complex dependency-heavy tasks like code modeling and distillation.
method: Benchmark three leading subquadratic architectures: xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet.
Evaluate them on challenging sequence tasks, including code-model pre-training and distillation from large language models.
Compare scalability and effectiveness to identify architectural principles that matter beyond raw efficiency.
impact: For practitioners, this helps narrow the design space for efficient sequence models and informs which architectures are worth adopting for long-context or code-related workloads. It provides evidence-based guidance for trading off accuracy, speed, and scalability.
visual_elements: Side-by-side architecture comparison diagram for xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet
Task pipeline graphic showing pre-training and distillation workflows
Bar chart comparing performance vs. compute/memory usage
Icon-based summary of long-context efficiency and dependency handling
paper_title: On Subquadratic Architectures: From Applications to Principles
paper_authors: Anamaria-Roberta Hartl, Levente Zólyomi, David Stap, Pieter-Jan Hoedt, Niklas Schmidinger
